look.why: Golden savanna grass, so the black-and-white stripes pop.

size.measure: nose to tail tip: head and body 2.17–2.46 m plus a 0.47–0.56 m tail

habitat.text: Open savannas and grasslands of eastern and southern Africa, up to 4,400 m.

diet.text: Mostly grass stems, about 90 % of what it eats, plus the odd herb, leaf or twig.

facts.text: Biting flies struggle to land on stripes, so zebras get bitten less than horses!
No two zebras have the same stripes, just like fingerprints.
